Love this machine! I was so tired of the new HE washers that I wanted to go back to the old school kind. This machine provides that. It is very heavy and solid. I can fill with water and get clothes cleaner than ever. No problems with mildew smells and cleaning cycles like HE washers.

Only had it for about a month now, but love it.  Why?  Well, we had a Kenmore which had an F-28 code that I fixed about 15 times (yea, that's right), and which I finally could not fix.  And, the wife and I wanted to return to a simpler washer, no electronics.  And, from what I read on the internet, this washer is built to last.  My wife says she loves it, and the matching dryer.  And I love my wife.
as old school as your going to find.and dang it cleans your clothes ! no bells no flashy lights just real clean clothes

I bought my Speed Queen washer at a local store, but the price was comparable to Amazon. I bought a Kenmore set 4 years ago and they've both gone out. The washer was top of the line and horrible at cleaning and it literally took me 2 hours to do a load of laundry. I was so glad when it finally died! Have had my Speed Queen 2 days and LOVE it. It is just the basic, no bells and whistles. I can control how much water goes in the machine and my clothes are clean in 20-30 minutes. The agitator and an adequate amount of water is the trick to cleaning clothes. Highly recommend this machine!

Quick. Fast. And easy. The simplicity of the design is beautiful. I love that it can power through a mountain of laundry in no time, 30 minutes to wash 30 to dry, or less, and a big load of laundry is folded and put away in 1 hour or less. Clean and fresh smelling. It doesn't hook into a computer, doesn't sing cute little tunes, no flashy gimmicky lights, no mildewy smell, uses WATER, no control temp regulators, AND CLOTHES ARE CLEAN first time around!!!! What more could you ask for??!!

Getting my laundry clean and not having to wait 90 minutes to go to bed at night because We need certain clothes the next day is worth any cost of some extra water.
Having reviewed and owned several over the past few years, this one is sturdy and built to last. It runs smoothly and definitely has quality.

I get my clothes DIRTY; landscaping, installing insulation, etc.  I bought a cheaper Whirlpool HE washing machine and tried it for three weeks. Returned it, salesman said a more expensive HE machine would do the job.  Tried it, returned it. I followed washing instructions exactly. Used HE detergent, in the water first..... If you work in an office and maybe just get a little sweat in your clothes I think the HE machines would be perfect for you.  But if you get serious dirt on you then they aren't worth crap, IMO.  I know they save water, but water is plentiful here and not that expensive.  Maybe HE is better for drought stricken areas.  And I don't really save much water when I have to wash the clothes twice.  (Just like my wonderful water saving toilet...which I have to flush twice. LOL).  Besides not cleaning well, they make an annoying growling sound (that's all I can call it) while washing, and two rinse cycles is minimum.  I do have very hard water here and that may play a role, but it doesn't affect how the Speed Queen performs.  This machine washes all the insulation fuzz off my clothes, takes our all the serious dirt, and doesn't make much noise in the process.  The lid doesn't lock down, so it's very quick to toss in more clothes.  (No having to hit the pause button and wait for it to release the lock). We bought this washer a year ago;  not sure if I ever reviewed....but I LOVE this washer! Now, it certainly has had some test of time.  After having a Maytag washer & dryer last 30 years, I anticipated good results with our second set.  Not so.......one broke down after 10 years doing light laundry for 2 retirees! We researched the Speed Queen as my father-in-law sold them years ago, and swore by them. So, this basic machine had the features I wanted, and the price was much more affordable.  This machine is great......washes well, uses the green detergent, is QUIET! My last Maytag sounded like percussion when spinning!  I'd highly recommend this washer; the bin is large, the cycle is not lengthy like my daughter's LG, it does not have a lot of electronic controls to have one go, and then the entire washer needs replacing.  Again, this washing machine does the job, and well! I'd give it a good look if you're researching new machines.

We have owned a Speed Queen washer for 2 1/2 years now and we love it because it cleans clothes quickly.  We can easily do eight or nine loads of laundry (washed AND dried) in a single day.  Try that with the so-called high efficiency machines.  NOW it isn't perfect - it's a traditional top loader with traditional issues.  It uses a lot of water.  It's a bit noisier.  It may not hold that california king size comforter.  Its agitator can damage clothes (especially if you overfill it with stuff and/or don't add enough water.)  It may not spin clothes as dry as a front loader (although mine seems to do a good enough job.)  Now what it DOES is clean your clothes.  And depending on load size (a setting which you NOT a computer determines) it does it in about 20 minutes (unless you use the second rinse option which is seldom needed.)  That's why we love our Speed Queen.
Amazing! It's everything I've been searching in for a washer. If it's not broken don't fix it. This machine has a much missed old fashion agitator.  10 ☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆

Will keep you updated, but if you buy online, YOU DO NOT HAVE A WARRANTY!

The size of cooktop was sufficient and stable when sitting on counter top. Power cord was long and didn't need to extend it. It's looks are on part with others and the controls are on the glass which is good. Some units place their buttons under a layer of plastic which, over time, will defiantly crack and malfunction.

More about the controls:
The size of the buttons is large and easy to read. However, disappointments included: The 10 predetermined temps were too broad and foods were either not warm enough on warm or started frying on next higher setting. If things got too hot and you needed to turn it off for a moment it totally resets to HIGH heat next time you turn it on. My previous model "remembered" any settings as long as it was kept plugged. I like to cook by temperature but every time you start cooking again it defaults back to cooking by watts and at the highest setting. Maybe they do with with the intention to cause people to say "wow, it gets hot so fast."

"Child Lock System" is a false claim as
the lock is worthless - it only locks the unit "ON" and if turned OFF it won't prevent the unit from turning ON. Every time I have wiped the unit to clean up after cooking it turns on so easily (and to the high setting).

This is the device to own if you enjoy burning your food. I've been a serious home cook for ten years. I know several dishes that I don't know where I got them, they've been tweaked, and I've even forgot the amounts, I just know what it's supposed to look like. All of this to say:

I've burned, or severely over cooked, everything I've made on this thing so far, and I've never been more excited.

The food is cooking too quickly. The pans heat too fast. All the rules the chefs say are starting to make sense.
1. Don't overcrowd the pan. Food to close to each other can trap the moisture and cause it to boil. So instead of frying your food, you're boiling it which dries the meat and slows the cooking. I've watched this happen on the cooktop.

2. Be at one station at a time. Used to be I could do dishes while I waited for food to cook, which is advice you'll see in several home magazines. Turns out it's only good advice for home cooks with crummy electric coils. This cooktop will over cook your food in a minute.

3. Use a food thermometer. Use temperature to cook, not by time or sight. I used to cut food to see if it was done. One just doesn't have time with this cooktop. And it's the only way to get a clear idea where the food is at. I used to use timers. The induction heating makes the type of pan matter. Cast iron is amazing. This is a great device in my opinion. I bought a cheap case for it, B00DSGGBVA, it works well without being overly large.

If you’re new to the idea of induction cooktops, I recommend viewing two vids on You Tube,
the first is Y6h0cqaqObA, after 9:20, where it shows the cyclical pulsation as the unit (not the Ivation, but similar) attempts to follow its thermostat. The other is xN8LCQq2_GY, after 2:00, where the localized heat input is pronounced.

The main problem with these, according to negative reviews, is the inability to simmer. When the Ivation first comes on, one ‘select’ press sets it to level 3. If you want to cook at a simmer, switch to temp mode. I tested this at the lowest temp mode, 140. After letting it heat 3 cups of water for 6 minutes, I took temps every minute and found the following temps: 168,162,156,150,145,160,155,149,161,156. You can see the pattern. If this gap is too wide for your style of low temp cooking, don’t go with induction. Look at ceramic infrared.
